title: Latency contour sculptor and kernel matchmaking for continuous batching
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Problem: We observe persistent 95/99th token latency spikes for heterogeneous workloads despite batching heuristics. Root causes identified: (1) kernel mismatch — requests with different sequence-length profiles and attention patterns pick suboptimal kernels leading to poor occupancy, (2) noisy admission — admission control treats all prefill/decodes equally causing bursty tails, (3) decode/prefill interference — long prefill requests block short decodes due to static slot reservation.

Goal: Implement a combined approach that (A) shapes admission based on a latency-contour model (the 'Latency Contour Sculptor'), (B) performs lightweight kernel matchmaking so runtime groups requests to kernel-compatible cohorts before packing, and (C) introduces a decode-aware prefill scheduler that isolates short-living decode jobs from long prefill jobs while preserving batching efficiency. The overall aim is to reduce 95/99th latency by 30-50% on mixed-production traces without increasing average cost per token by >5%.
acceptance_criteria: 95th token latency reduced by >=30% on mixed-prod trace (baseline: 420ms -> <=294ms)
99th token latency reduced by >=35% on same trace
P95/P99 improvements hold for both streaming and non-streaming routes
No increase in mean cost-per-token >5% measured over 72h rolling window
Feature has rollout flags and observability: per-route kernel assignments, contour histograms, and admission-reject metrics
work_items: design latency-contour model: quantile sketch per tenant + lightweight bucketizer
implement kernel matchmaking shim in admission path (GPU-side hints)
prefill/decode priority scheduler: slot fast-path for short decodes
integration tests and microbench harness for mixed sequences
dashboard panels for contour heatmaps and kernel-cohort distributions
gradual rollout plan with canary and kill-switch
technical_notes:
Design notes: 1) Latency contour uses streaming quantile sketches (TDigest) per route to estimate sequence-length and attention-sparsity quantiles; sketches emitted to control-plane every 5m. 2) Bucketizer maps incoming request to one of 6 latency-contour buckets; admission favors filling batches with same bucket to improve kernel locality. 3) Kernel matchmaking uses a two-byte hint (kernel_id_hint) appended to admission token; admission layer prefers matches where kernel_id_hint is equal or 'compatible' (precomputed compatibility matrix). 4) Prefill scheduler introduces a 'decode-fastlane' token slot: requests with expected decode length < 32 tokens or marked as interactive are sent to fastlane to avoid head-of-line blocking. 5) Backpressure: if fastlane fills, decode requests can opportunistically merge into neighbor buckets but with a maximum wait of 8ms. 6) Safety: all changes behind runtime feature flag and route-level opt-in.

Trade-offs considered: stronger bucketization increases kernel utilization but risks increased queueing for large-batch kernels; compatibility matrix must be compact to avoid admission overhead. Chosen to start with conservative 6 buckets and evolve with telemetry.

Microbench results (simulated mixed trace): average latency +2%, p95 -36%, p99 -41%, GPU utilization +5%, tokens/sec unchanged. Test harness: github.com/redwood/runtime/compare/eng/ENG-100512-microbench (private PR).
implementation_plan: Week 1: Kernel hint shim + compatibility matrix (Nic).
Week 2: Prefill/decode fastlane and admission policy knobs (Maya + Priya).
Week 3: Integration tests, load tests on perf-cluster, telemetry wiring (SRE).
Week 4: Canary rollout to 5% of production traffic, observe metrics 72h, iterate.
Rollout: 5% -> 25% -> 60% -> 100% with automatic rollback on SLO regressions
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Over-bucketization leads to starvation of rare kernels. Mitigation: Global fallback bucket and max-wait expiry to allow reallocation.
Risk: Compatibility matrix becomes stale as kernels change. Mitigation: Compatibility generation job tied to release pipeline; compatibility version included in model artifact.
Risk: Telemetry overhead from per-route sketches. Mitigation: sampling (1/10 routes) and 5m aggregation windows; ability to disable per-route sketches.
Risk: Increased control-plane churn. Mitigation: limit sketch emission frequency and batch updates to control-plane write queue.
